transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. It's really nice to meet you. 

Um, well... my wife actually thought it would be a good idea for me to talk to someone. Is it okay if I start there? I guess I've just been... really productive lately. Which is usually a good thing, right? But I kind of can't seem to stop launching new projects. I've been drafting all these new work plans, setting up aggressive schedules for new IT certifications, completely overhauling our home network, sending out messages to a bunch of old contacts... just staying really, really busy. 

I think I just get a little too focused, maybe? It gets pretty intense, and I guess I tend to blow past normal limits—just working straight through without realizing it—until my wife or my director at work has to step in and sort of tell me to hit the brakes. I really don't mean to cause any stress for them, I just get so driven to get things done. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
When this happens, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual?

Well, um... I guess I do sleep a little less during those times. But it doesn't feel like a bad thing, you know? Like, there have been runs where I maybe only get about three hours of sleep, and I'll wake up right at 3 or 4 a.m. 

But I don't feel exhausted or anything. I actually feel really sharp. It's almost like... like I've been handed this extra bonus time to get a head start on my day, instead of feeling tired. I mean, getting more hours in the day to be productive is a positive thing, right? I hope that doesn't sound too strange... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
During these periods, do you feel unusually euphoric or overly confident?

Um, well... I wouldn't necessarily use the word "euphoric." Maybe just really... enthusiastic? I mean, I take a lot of pride in my work, so feeling good about what I do is normal, right? 

But I guess, regarding the confidence part... if I'm being completely honest, maybe it does get a little high. Like, sometimes when I get in that zone, I start to feel like... well, I guess at my worst, I honestly start to believe that I'm the absolute *only* person who can see the whole network architecture clearly. I get this really intense feeling that if people would just step back and follow my plan, I could save the company from a major failure. 

I know that probably sounds a bit arrogant saying it out loud, and I really don't mean to be difficult with my team or my director. I just want to help the company succeed, you know? Does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm not coming across as too full of myself...
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day?

Um... well... I guess everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? I try really hard to stay positive, especially for my wife, because she does so much for us. But... if I'm being completely honest, yeah, there have been times like that. 

It's actually kind of embarrassing to admit, but there are stretches where I wake up feeling like... well, like a failed version of myself. Everything just feels really heavy and flat. I feel terrible about it because I want to be a good partner, but during those weeks, even just answering my wife’s normal, everyday questions feels like it's just too much. Like it takes all my energy just to respond to her. 

I know I should just snap out of it when it happens, and I really try to. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information... is that what you were asking about?
During those high-energy periods, have you ever had to be hospitalized because of them?

Um, hospitalized? No, no, definitely not. I've never had to go to the hospital for anything like that. 

I mean, sure, I might get a little intense about my work sometimes, but it's never gotten out of hand to the point where I'd need to be admitted anywhere. I'm always able to keep things under control and, you know, still do my job and be at home. 

I really wouldn't want anyone to think I'm unstable or anything like that. I'm just very passionate about what I do when I get in that mode. Does that answer your question? I hope that's okay.
During those high-energy periods, do they ever cause serious problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Um... well, "serious problems" sounds a bit... strong, I guess? I mean, I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly. But... I suppose, if I'm looking at it objectively, there have been some... hiccups. 

At work, for instance... there was this one project, a migration, and I had this really clear vision for it, but it didn't quite pan out the way I planned. They actually asked me to take a little leave of absence after that. Just to recharge, you know? I think they just wanted me to rest, really. 

And at home... well, my wife is wonderful, she really is. She's just had to... help me manage things a bit more during those times. Like keeping an eye on our spending, or gently reminding me to stop working at 3 AM. Sometimes we do end up bickering a little because I get so focused, but I really don't mean to upset her. 

I've also... well, I used to be really involved with the music at our church, and I loved rock climbing and mentoring junior staff. But lately, I've had to step back from all of that. It's just hard to be consistent and show up when my energy is so... unpredictable. 

I feel awful about letting people down. I really want to be reliable. Does that... does that count as what you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is...
